message.content: At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**. This is a modest depression compared with the 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm, reflecting the fact that the solid–liquid equilibrium shifts to lower temperatures as the external pressure is reduced.
